brief: Goldman's equities desk reports a defensive US session on 10 September 2026. Rising oil and yields drove angst into Thursday's CPI: WTI breached $100 and the 10-year hit 4.90%, its highest since November 2023, with September hike estimates at 70%. Softer topline PPI still left PCE-relevant categories firmer, so the desk raised its August core PCE estimate to 0.24% from 0.22%. Equities fell across the board, S&P -58bps at 7,591 with a $1.65bn MOC to sell, breadth poor at 331 decliners, and a 26th straight session of sub-1% intraday ranges, the longest in five years. Positioning turned defensive, with Telco/Cable, Staples and REITs higher against Semis, AI Infra and beta, and AAPL plus megacaps catching a relative bid. Hedge funds and long-onlys each finished $1bn net sellers. In vol, NDX and SPX skew were bid across the curve, dealer long gamma now sits to the topside which the desk says frees spot to move down, and it likes IWM September puts as a CPI hedge. ORCL rose 7% after hours on a beat, an FY27 guidance raise, a completed $20bn ATM and over $30bn of AI Cloud contracts.
